connector.name: Crowdsentinel MCP Server
connector.registryDescription: AI threat hunting & incident response for Elasticsearch/OpenSearch with endpoint & network forensics
connector.summary: Runs locally from the Python package crowdsentinel-mcp-server. Needs an API key you supply, and it reaches 8 of 9 clients tracked here.
connector.provenanceNote: Published from the thomasxm account, and the linked repository sits under the same account. Namespace ownership was proven at publish time.
connector.authNote: A long lived key or token is required. Scope it as narrowly as the upstream service allows and rotate it on a schedule.

env.name: ELASTICSEARCH_HOSTS
env.description: Comma-separated Elasticsearch hosts. Supports HTTP/HTTPS, local/remote/cloud (e.g., http://localhost:9200, https://es.prod.example.com:9200)

env.name: ELASTICSEARCH_CLOUD_ID
env.description: Elastic Cloud deployment ID (alternative to ELASTICSEARCH_HOSTS for cloud deployments)

env.name: ELASTICSEARCH_API_KEY
env.description: API key for authentication (recommended for production and Elastic Cloud)

env.name: ELASTICSEARCH_USERNAME
env.description: Username for basic authentication (alternative to API key)

env.name: ELASTICSEARCH_PASSWORD
env.description: Password for basic authentication (used with ELASTICSEARCH_USERNAME)

env.name: ELASTICSEARCH_BEARER_TOKEN
env.description: Bearer/service token for authentication (alternative to API key)

env.name: VERIFY_CERTS
env.description: TLS certificate verification: true (verify CA — production), false (skip — dev/test), or /path/to/ca.crt (custom CA)
